papers.title: The Last AI Built by Humans: Toward Genuine Recursive Self-Improvement
papers.summary: Distinguishes execution, strategy, experience, environment, and meta-improvement autonomy; a roadmap is not evidence that this repository reaches the final level.

papers.title: Evo2: Evolving the Evolver through Weight-Harness Co-Evolution
papers.summary: Joint proposer/reflector harness search and SFT/GRPO weight updates. Ouroboros exports reviewable code proposals, but does not reproduce EvoTIDE or its coding-benchmark results.

papers.title: Are Self-Evolving Agents Continual Learners?
papers.summary: Finds a plasticity/stability tradeoff even for nonparametric harness and memory updates. Motivates comparisons with both the original and latest accepted generation.

papers.title: Sparks of Weight-Space Programming: LLMs can natively read & write neural network weights
papers.authors: Rikiya Takehi and Jayden Teoh and Alex Zhang and Omar Khattab
papers.summary: MIT CSAIL reports an Astra edit of Qwen3.5-0.8B: MATH-500 7.9% to 48.1%, with 50 forward passes and 131072 edited entries. Not a Harvard paper, not gradient training, and not an Ouroboros result.

papers.title: Can an LLM Actually Reason and Program about Neural Network's Weights or is it just memorization on steroids? Exploring "Weight-Space Programming"
papers.summary: An exploratory reading audit finds local arithmetic plus dataset priors; label permutation controls undermine stronger semantic-reading claims. Does not refute every editing result.

papers.title: Exploring Weight-Space Programming: Capabilities, Generalization, and Limitations
papers.summary: Six of sixteen trajectories retain the original weights; gains and transfer vary. The 29.45-point MATH-500 result is author-reported, not reproduced here. Upstream checkout currently contains a PDF only.

papers.title: Interpretable weight-space programming builds transparent transformers and brain encoding models
papers.summary: Studies directly coded interpretable computations for small networks and scientific encoding tasks. This is not a general algorithm for autonomously growing a deployed LLM.

papers.title: WeightBench: Evaluating Language Models as Weight-Space Programmers
papers.authors: Aayush Marasini and Barsat Khadka and Nick Rahimi
papers.summary: 42 tasks across reading, fixing, writing, impossible edits and data-free compression; abstract reports substantial limitations. Upstream OS-level harness is separate from Ouroboros unit tests.

papers.title: Replicating and Extending Weight-Space Programming: Frontier LLMs Compile Programs into Weights and Read Input Layers
papers.authors: Roksana Goworek and Alexander Hickey and Federico Nanni and Martin O'Reilly
papers.summary: Independent replication of small-network writing, with evidence for program compilation and shallow input-layer reading rather than unrestricted semantic understanding.

papers.title: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights
papers.summary: A 27B model reportedly gains 6.6 accuracy points on held-out math; smaller models abstain or damage themselves. Repeated practice checks are not an untouched final test. v2 dated November 18 was consulted.

discovery.pretrained_study_status: 135M running locally; 360M configured on GitHub, not yet verified

papers.title: Weight-Space Programming Doesn't Need Transformers
papers.summary: Agents choose sparse associative tables for directly written weights. Pretrained LLMs remain more accurate; the claim is about structures to build when writing weights, not replacing all Transformers.

papers.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
papers.summary: Low-rank trainable adapters over frozen base weights.

papers.title: Locating and Editing Factual Associations in GPT
papers.summary: Full ROME includes causal tracing, key/value optimization and covariance statistics. A generic rank-one update is not equivalent.

papers.title: STaR: Bootstrapping Reasoning With Reasoning
papers.summary: Correctness-filtered reasoning data with iterative fine-tuning; local export utilities implement only part of the algorithm.

papers.title: Mass-Editing Memory in a Transformer
papers.summary: Distributed multi-layer factual edits, requiring method-specific statistics and validation.

papers.title: Editing Models with Task Arithmetic
papers.summary: Extract and add/subtract task vectors; subtraction is not certified unlearning.

papers.title: Self-Instruct: Aligning Language Models with Self-Generated Instructions
papers.summary: Bootstrap tasks and filter generated examples. Trusted independent verification remains necessary.

papers.title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
papers.summary: Quantized base weights and LoRA adapters. CUDA/bitsandbytes support is opt-in and not GPU-tested in this sandbox.

papers.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
papers.summary: Optimize preferred versus rejected completions relative to a frozen reference policy.

papers.title: TIES-Merging: Resolving Interference When Merging Models
papers.summary: Trim, elect signs, and disjointly merge agreeing task-vector entries. Separate from DARE.

papers.title: Representation Engineering: A Top-Down Approach to AI Transparency
papers.summary: Read and intervene on representations; vector arithmetic alone does not install runtime model hooks.

papers.title: UltraFeedback: Boosting Language Models with High-quality Feedback
papers.summary: AI feedback for preference data; not proof that a model can reliably judge itself.

papers.title: Language Models are Super Mario: Absorbing Abilities from Homologous Models as a Free Lunch
papers.summary: DARE drops and rescales task-vector entries; this is not the TIES paper.

papers.title: Self-Play Fine-Tuning Converts Weak Language Models to Strong Language Models
papers.summary: Self-play alignment research; no learned minimax loop is claimed for fixed local adversarial fixtures.

papers.title: Self-Rewarding Language Models
papers.summary: Iterative self-generated preferences and DPO. A style-word heuristic is not a valid reproduction.

papers.title: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models
papers.summary: Introduces GRPO in a mathematical reasoning setting, after iterative domain mining and n-gram benchmark decontamination. Local status: GRPO is not implemented (group reward standardisation is recorded as arithmetic and labelled as such), while the decontamination direction is implemented in a narrower, stricter question-overlap admission screen that runs before any model load.

papers.title: Evolutionary Optimization of Model Merging Recipes
papers.summary: Searches merging recipes in parameter and data-flow spaces; shape-compatible layer copies are only a primitive.

papers.title: Large Language Monkeys: Scaling Inference Compute with Repeated Sampling
papers.summary: Repeated sampling makes verifier quality and equal-compute comparison critical.

papers.title: The AI Scientist: Towards Fully Automated Open-Ended Scientific Discovery
papers.summary: Automated research workflows; generated source must not share host credentials or evaluator authority.

papers.title: Darwin Godel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents
papers.summary: Empirical source-code self-improvement with an archive of agents; not the same as parametric self-rewriting.

papers.title: Self-Adapting Language Models
papers.summary: Generate self-edits and optimize them with an outer RL loop; local SFT does not reproduce that outer loop.

papers.title: SIA: Self Improving AI with Harness & Weight Updates
papers.summary: Co-updates an agent harness and weights; replaces the former unspecific 2025 homepage citation.

papers.title: AI models collapse when trained on recursively generated data
papers.summary: Motivates preserving real data and monitoring distribution drift; does not establish a universal 25% replay ratio or guarantee against forgetting.

papers.title: DeepSeek official research: source-linked applicability review
papers.summary: Nineteen pinned official repositories and selected method sections (62 documents, 13 PDFs) were read to decide what a bounded CPU research loop may adopt. Four bounded features were implemented, three only partially, and the rest were refused or deferred with reasons. No DeepSeek result is reproduced.

papers.title: DeepSeek LLM: Scaling Open-Source Language Models with Longtermism
papers.summary: Long-termism data mixture with multi-step versus cosine schedules, batch-size scaling and checkpoint cadence at 2T-token scale. Locally only the schedule/clipping/step-bookkeeping shape is reused and measured; no scaling law or large-batch conclusion is transplanted.

papers.title: DeepSeek Coder: Let the Code Write Itself
papers.summary: Repository-level code corpus with dependency-aware concatenation, near-deduplication and 50% fill-in-the-middle training in the 16B variant. FIM, repo mining and near-dedup are not implemented; only stricter anti-contamination admission is.

papers.title: DeepSeekMoE: Towards Ultimate Expert Specialization in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models
papers.summary: Fine-grained expert splitting plus always-on shared experts, with a higher activated count to preserve compute. Requires a genuine MoE architecture; no dense-to-MoE conversion exists here.

papers.title: DeepSeek-V2: A Strong, Economical, and Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Language Model
papers.summary: Multi-head Latent Attention with joint low-rank KV compression, decoupled RoPE and weight absorption, plus device-limited expert routing. Requires an MLA model; post-hoc KV compression of a dense model is a different method.

papers.title: DeepSeek-Coder-V2: Breaking the Barrier of Closed-Source Models in Code Intelligence
papers.summary: 6T-token continued pretraining over a 60% code / 10% math / 30% text mixture, with FIM in the 16B but not the 236B variant. Out of scope at CPU-fixture scale; the bounded data_reweight family is not a mixture re-pretraining stage.

papers.title: DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report
papers.summary: MoE model with auxiliary-loss-free expert bias, multi-token prediction sharing embeddings and head, and a long curriculum. Only audited training bookkeeping (constant/cosine schedules, clipping, per-step loss/gradient/optimizer/RSS records) is adapted; MTP, MoE and packing are not implemented.

papers.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Cold-start SFT, reasoning RL, then correctness-filtered rejection SFT and distillation. Only the verified-distillation shape is implemented, with an independent local teacher and exact-answer filtering; there is no RL stage and answer correctness does not certify a rationale.

papers.title: DeepSeek-Prover-V1.5: Harnessing Proof Assistant Feedback for Reinforcement Learning and Monte-Carlo Tree Search
papers.summary: Expert iteration over Lean-verified proofs with truncate-and-resume search and moderately solvable prompts for group optimization. The local loop borrows only the verification-first rollout/filter/re-evaluate shape; its verifier is exact-answer matching, not Lean, and adds no formal guarantee.

papers.title: DeepSeek-Prover-V2: Advancing Formal Mathematical Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning for Subgoal Decomposition
papers.summary: Verified subgoal decomposition used to build coarse-grained proof sketches for reinforcement learning. Deferred: without a proof assistant there is no subgoal prover, sketch or formal check.

papers.title: Expert Specialized Fine-Tuning
papers.summary: Selects task-relevant MoE experts from training gate/token statistics with a cumulative threshold, then tunes only those experts while all remain routable. Dense LoRA is not ESFT and no expert selection, gating or freezing exists here.

papers.title: DeepSeekMath-V2: Towards Self-Verifiable Mathematical Reasoning
papers.summary: Learned proof verifier scoring proofs, plus meta-verification that an alleged flaw actually exists to avoid rewarding hallucinated criticism. Deliberately refused: the foundation keeps an exact-answer grader and never lets a model score its own work.

papers.title: DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp: Boosting Long-Context Efficiency with DeepSeek Sparse Attention
papers.summary: Experimental DeepSeek Sparse Attention with a trained lightning indexer and top-k KV selection, using dense warm-up then joint sparse continued training. Deferred; pruning attention post hoc is explicitly not this method.

papers.title: Engram: Conditional Memory via Scalable Lookup
papers.summary: Trainable conditional memory from canonicalized suffix n-gram hashing with a learned context gate and depthwise causal convolution. The append-only SQLite ledger in this repository records experiments and never enters a forward pass, so it is not Engram.

papers.title: DeepSeek-VL: Towards Real-World Vision-Language Understanding
papers.summary: Hybrid vision encoders with modality warm-up, language-retention mixtures and explicit small-model limits. Deferred: no vision encoder, image-text data, warm-up stage or visual evaluator exists here.

papers.title: DeepSeek-VL2: Mixture-of-Experts Vision-Language Models for Advanced Multimodal Understanding
papers.summary: Dynamic image tiling with a global thumbnail and 2x2 pixel shuffle to reduce visual tokens, decoded by an MoE language model. Deferred; token-budget language elsewhere in this repository is unrelated to visual tiling.

papers.title: Janus-Pro: Unified Multimodal Understanding and Generation with Data and Model Scaling
papers.summary: Separate understanding and generation encodings under one autoregressive transformer with staged training and data mixtures. Deferred: no image tokenizer, generation head, image data or visual metrics; proposer/executor/evaluator separation is not a multimodal architecture.

papers.title: DeepSeek-OCR: Contexts Optical Compression
papers.summary: Optical context compression: convolutional visual token reduction, a global vision encoder and an MoE decoder across multiple resolution modes. Deferred; local output-byte and checkpoint bounding is unrelated compression.

papers.title: DeepSeek-OCR-2: Visual Causal Flow
papers.summary: Replaces a global vision encoder with a bidirectional visual prefix from a small causal LM and routes only causal flow queries into the decoder. Deferred; no visual encoder, query routing, image data or decoding experiments exist here.
